axes_unresolved: comparison with the fixed sensor mosaic; counterbalanced imagery and reading order; articulatory EMG; seed repetition; vowel decoding on non-overlapping onset-aligned epochs
technical_limits: The task labels are ISP-versus-silence, ISP-versus-silent-reading, and /a/, /e/, /i/ vowel classes. The binary contrast can reflect task engagement, attention, or residual sensorimotor activity, as the authors acknowledge. Closed-set epoch classification does not establish word/sentence decoding or speech reconstruction; SAP and LOSO have different generalization meanings.
evaluation_limits: The cohort is 21 neurotypical native French speakers after excluding five of 26 participants, and stimuli use a closed, cued syllable/sentence paradigm. Subject-Agnostic Pooled (SAP) uses trial-grouped 10-fold cross-validation and must not be read as subject-independent; Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) is the separate held-out-participant protocol. The main content task is three-vowel classification, not word or sentence decoding. The authors note that task engagement, attention, or residual sensorimotor activity could contribute to ISP-versus-silence discrimination and that vowel scores are below practical speech-BCI requirements. Online, clinical, naturalistic, and continuous-speech evaluation is absent.
deployment_limits: The paper evaluates offline classification of recorded MEG epochs. It reports no real-time or online interface, continuous speech decoding, user communication study, portable implementation, latency, or deployment measurement. The recording uses a 248-magnetometer MEG system.
scope_limits: Twenty-one neurotypical native French participants after exclusions; cued, closed-set sentence/syllable tasks; two condition contrasts and three-vowel classification. No continuous sentence transcription, open-vocabulary decoding, speech synthesis, clinical cohort, online use, or user communication outcome.
input_modality: Magnetoencephalography (MEG), recorded with 248 magnetometers at 1 kHz; non-invasive.
sensor_hardware: MEG recorded at 1 kHz with 248 magnetometers; device make/model is not specified in the reviewed text.
vocabulary_type: Cued French sentence imagery and closed-set three-vowel labels; no open vocabulary or continuous text output.
vocabulary_size: Closed set of 18 syllable items combining one of five consonants or none with one of three vowels; the distinct sentence-set size is not separately specified beyond three blocks of 34 sentence trials.
metrics: Full-window ResNet-18 balanced accuracy (mean ± 95% CI): ISP vs silence 90.4 ± 2.5% SAP and 77.5 ± 1.3% LOSO; ISP vs silent reading 81.0 ± 2.0% SAP and 72.2 ± 1.5% LOSO; three-vowel decoding 60.6 ± 1.5% SAP and 51.7 ± 0.8% LOSO (three-class chance 33%). SAP is trial-grouped pooled 10-fold CV; LOSO is participant-held-out. Table 4's no-pretraining convolutional/random-initialization/partial-fine-tuning variant reports 81.6/70.8% for ISP-vs-silence, 72.1/64.9% for ISP-vs-silent-reading, and 53.3/46.0% for vowels (SAP/LOSO).
evaluation_mode: Offline balanced-accuracy classification with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. The paper compares LDA, EEGNet, a shallow CNN, a Riemannian tangent-space classifier, ResNet-18, and ViT-Tiny across pre-cue, post-cue, and full (-300 to 500 ms) windows. It reports stratified 10-fold SAP grouped by trial and a distinct 21-fold leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocol; pairwise model tests use Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and comparisons against chance use permutation tests, with Holm-Bonferroni correction stated.

evidence.statement: The abstract presents an image-based MEG approach that maps imagined-speech signals to time-frequency representations for ImageNet-pretrained vision models, and reports three task families: imagery versus silence, imagery versus silent reading, and vowel decoding.

Twenty-six neurotypical native French speakers took part and five were excluded, leaving 21. The paradigm used three blocks of 34 sentences (6–11 syllables), a closed set of 18 syllable items, silent reading followed by imagery at 400 ms per syllable, and 248-channel MEG recorded at 1 kHz.
evidence.section_or_location: Section 2.1, Dataset and tasks; PDF p. 1

evidence.statement: Preprocessing includes 50/100/150 Hz notch filters, a 0.5–150 Hz band-pass, downsampling to 500 Hz, ICA and AutoReject artifact handling, and pre-cue (-300 to 0 ms), post-cue (0 to 500 ms), and full (-300 to 500 ms) epochs; silence examples come from inter-trial rest, not inter-syllable gaps.
evidence.section_or_location: Section 2.2, Preprocessing and epoch extraction; PDF p. 2

evidence.statement: The representation applies Morlet CWT independently to each channel at 96 log-spaced frequencies from 1 to 150 Hz, then uses a learnable 1×1 sensor-space projection to mix 248 channel scalograms into three maps and resizes the result to 224×224×3 for the vision models.

The evaluation distinguishes Subject-Agnostic Pooled stratified 10-fold cross-validation grouped by trial from a separate Leave-One-Subject-Out protocol with 21 folds; balanced accuracy is used, with 50% binary and 33% three-class chance levels.
evidence.section_or_location: Evaluation protocol in Section 2.5; PDF p. 3

evidence.statement: For full-window ISP-versus-silence decoding, ResNet-18 reports 90.4 ± 2.5% SAP and 77.5 ± 1.3% LOSO balanced accuracy; SAP is pooled trial-grouped evaluation and LOSO is the participant-held-out result.
evidence.section_or_location: Section 3.1, Table 1 and Fig. 3; PDF p. 3

evidence.statement: For full-window ISP-versus-silent-reading decoding, ResNet-18 reports 81.0 ± 2.0% SAP and 72.2 ± 1.5% LOSO balanced accuracy; the text identifies this contrast as more difficult than ISP versus silence.
evidence.section_or_location: Section 3.2, Table 2 and Fig. 4; PDF p. 3

evidence.statement: For full-window three-class /a/, /e/, /i/ decoding, ResNet-18 reports 60.6 ± 1.5% SAP and 51.7 ± 0.8% LOSO balanced accuracy; the separate post-cue LOSO table entry is 51.4 ± 0.9% and should not be substituted for the full-window value.
evidence.section_or_location: Section 3.3 and Table 3, PDF p. 3; Fig. 5, PDF p. 4

evidence.statement: In the full-window ablation, the convolutional-projection model with random initialization and partial fine-tuning reports SAP/LOSO balanced accuracy of 81.6/70.8% for ISP versus silence, 72.1/64.9% for ISP versus silent reading, and 53.3/46.0% for vowel decoding, below the pretrained baseline entries.

The discussion says ISP-versus-silence decoding may be influenced by broader task engagement, attention, or residual sensorimotor activity, and that current vowel accuracy remains below what would be required for practical speech BCIs; future work includes larger phonemic sets and adaptive timing.

The conclusion describes an image-driven MEG decoding strategy and imagery-locked discriminative information, while framing it as a foundation for future non-invasive speech decoding studies rather than reporting a communication interface or sentence transcription result.

en.summary: ImageNet transfer on MEG scalograms (M03) and the learned sensor projection (M06) are standard; the ablation is new; rest and reading-order confounds limit the binary tasks (M12).
en.sensor: 248-magnetometer MEG (non-invasive)
en.task: Closed-set imagined speech condition and vowel classification
en.speaker: Both
en.key_result: ResNet-18 full-window balanced accuracy: imagery vs silence 90.4% pooled / 77.5% LOSO; imagery vs silent reading 81.0% / 72.2%; three vowels 60.6% / 51.7% (chance 33%). Removing ImageNet weights costs 5.7-8.9 points.
en.limitations: ImageNet transfer on MEG scalograms was done before (Dash et al. 2020, cited only for imagined sentences); binary tasks contrast imagery with rest and with silent reading in fixed order; no EMG; no seeds; learned projection not compared with a sensor mosaic; offline only.

title: Zero-Shot Imagined Speech Decoding via Imagined-to-Listened MEG Mapping
expert_take_short: New pipeline (imagined MEG mapped to listened MEG, then a listened-trained word decoder), but no no-mapping or null-mapping word control, and a shared closed poem set confounds word decoding.
expert_take_long: The paper changes the decoding route (M06), the training regime (M03) and the recording (M11), all standard against the field, and under-reports its word-level evaluation (M12). Composing an imagined-to-listened mapping with a listened-trained decoder is new only as a pipeline among 112 pattern-matched studies (the authors' earlier mapping decodes nothing), and stays standard because no control passes unmapped imagined MEG or a null-mapping output through the decoder, so the mapping's contribution to word retrieval is not shown. Every participant imagines the same two poems whose 76 words form the candidate set, so poem identity alone lifts ranks above chance; zero-shot holds across subjects, not across stimuli.
expert_true_value: A new pipeline for imagined speech (imagined MEG mapped into listened-response space, then a decoder trained only on listened MEG), evaluated on held-out subjects; its word-level gain over direct transfer is not measured.
canon_before: Imagery decoding transferred decoders across conditions directly (MEG melody classifiers trained on imagery and tested on listening, 2023; an overt-trained ECoG Transformer applied to covert speech, 46.3% token error rate, 2024); the authors' 2025 study mapped imagined onto listened MEG without decoding content; intracortical decoders trained on inner plus attempted speech reached 14-33% word error rate on inner speech over 50 words (2025).
delta_from_canon: Composes six imagined-to-listened mapping models with a frozen contrastive word decoder trained on listened MEG, and ranks 76 poem words from imagined MEG of subjects unseen by both stages.
position_in_field: Standard on the decoding route (M06; new only as a pipeline), on zero-shot cross-subject training (M03), on the recording (M11) and on the laboratory setting (M13); word-level evaluation (M12) not reported well enough: no no-mapping or null-mapping control, no named test, post hoc top-20 subsets.
practical_value: Low: offline, closed set of 76 words from two memorized poems, bidirectional mapping, laboratory MEG.
axes_moved: decoding route: imagined-to-listened mapping before a listened-trained decoder; held-out-subject evaluation without calibration
axes_unresolved: word-level control without the mapping or with a null mapping; held-out poems; per-subject Recall@k over all 76 words; seeds and decoder split unit; analysed N (17 recruited, 13 shown)
technical_limits: Mapping prediction correlations are small; four stimuli; 76-word closed vocabulary; encoder differences vanish in the full pipeline; the appendix transformer is at chance.
evaluation_limits: Word retrieval compared only with analytic chance 1/76 and a listened ceiling; Fig. 4A significance has no named test; Figs. A5-A6 use post hoc top-20 words; 4-class p for raw imagined MEG is 0.10 in the text and 0.12 in the caption; decoder validation and test partitions unstated.
deployment_limits: Offline laboratory MEG; bidirectional RNN mapping; no online, confirmation or correction test.
scope_limits: Trained musicians imagining two Bach chorales and two poem excerpts; the same stimuli for all participants, so zero-shot holds across subjects, not across stimuli or words.
input_modality: magnetic
sensor_hardware: Whole-head KIT MEG, 157 axial gradiometers
vocabulary_type: Closed set of content words from the two poems used in training and test
metrics: Mapping: per-channel Pearson r against a pairing-shuffle null (paired t; RNN LOSO t = 9.59). Listened decoder: Recall@1/5/10 (BERT+Wav2Vec2 0.091/0.351/0.541). Full pipeline: rank curves and normalized area above chance, no single number.
evaluation_mode: Leave-one-subject-out for mapping and decoder; shuffled-pairing null for the mapping only; word-level pipeline compared with analytic chance; offline.

evidence.statement: The authors claim a paired imagined-listened MEG dataset, six mapping models that generalize to unseen subjects, and above-chance zero-shot word decoding from imagined MEG (Sec. 1).

Composing an imagined-to-listened mapping with a listened-trained word decoder is new only as a pipeline among 112 pattern-matched cross-condition studies; the only earlier mapping study, by the same authors, decodes no content.

17 musicians were recruited and imagined or heard two melodies and two poems, 10 trials of 27 s per condition; Fig. A7 shows 13 held-out subjects; the 76 candidate words come from the same two poems (Sec. 2.1, 2.4).

All six mappings beat a pairing-shuffle null on held-out subjects (RNN t = 9.59); predicted-listened responses classify the four stimuli at 34% against 30% for raw imagined MEG, with no test of the difference (Table 2, Sec. 3.2).
Listened-only decoder Recall@1/5/10 is 0.091/0.351/0.541 for BERT+Wav2Vec2 and 0.086/0.365/0.550 for BERT; the full pipeline is reported only as rank curves above 1/76 (Table 3, Fig. 4A).
No control passes unmapped imagined MEG or a null-mapping output through the decoder, Fig. 4A names no test, and per-model breakdowns use post hoc top-20 words (Sec. 3.4, Appendix D.1).
The study is offline with a bidirectional RNN mapping and laboratory MEG; the abstract's claim of direct applicability to realistic BCIs is untested.
The authors call the work a proof of concept and attribute the gap to the listened ceiling to small mapping correlations and a small vocabulary (Discussion).

en.summary: New pipeline (imagined MEG mapped to listened MEG, then a listened-trained word decoder), but no no-mapping or null-mapping word control, and a shared closed poem set confounds word decoding.
en.sensor: 157-channel whole-head MEG
en.speaker: Speaker-independent
en.key_result: Recall@1 up to ~9.1% (combined embeddings), 76 words, leave-one-subject-out
en.limitations: Small 76-word vocabulary from rhythmic stimuli by trained musicians; low SNR; non-portable MEG; not tested on natural continuous imagined speech.

title: A Convolutional Framework for Mapping Imagined Auditory MEG into Listened Brain Responses
venue: 2025 59th Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers
expert_take_short: Mapping imagined onto listened MEG (M06) is ahead in design, but the subject-calibrated CNN gain is unproven: no ablation, a channel-shuffling null, and r 0.0113 against 0.0063.
expert_take_long: The paper changes M06 (ahead: no earlier imagined-to-listened neural mapping among 112 ledger studies, pattern match), M03 (standard: subject-layer recipe refitted on the held-out subject) and M11 (standard). Its claim that the calibrated CNN generalizes where linear mappings fail lacks controls; the null shuffles channels, and the authors' own later study finds a linear mapping transfers without calibration.
expert_true_value: Introduces imagined-to-listened neural mapping (M06), with no earlier example among 112 pattern-matched studies; the calibrated-CNN evidence is weak (r 0.0113 vs 0.0063, channel-shuffling null, no ablation).
canon_before: Work linking imagery and perception transferred decoders between conditions (MEG melody classifiers trained on imagery and tested on listening, 2023; overt-trained ECoG Transformers applied to covert speech, 2024); pooled M/EEG decoders used a per-subject 1x1 subject layer (2022).
delta_from_canon: Regresses whole imagined MEG responses onto listened ones, first per subject with ridge regression, then with a pooled encoder-decoder temporal CNN whose per-subject 1x1 calibration layer is refitted on part of the held-out subject.
position_in_field: Ahead on the mapping target (M06), standard on pooled training with a subject layer (M03) and on the recording (M11); superseded by the authors' 2026 follow-up on the same paradigm, where six mappings, including a linear one, beat a pairing-only null on unseen subjects without calibration and a nonlinear RNN separates most.
practical_value: Low: four stimuli and no content decoded from the predicted responses.
axes_moved: decoding target: imagined-to-listened neural mapping
axes_unresolved: calibration-layer ablation; pairing-only null with intact channels; repeated shuffles and seeds; content decoding from predicted responses; calibration subset size and disjointness
technical_limits: Four stimuli; 0.1-8 Hz, seven DSS components, 100 Hz; 155-channel CNN input against 157 recorded channels, with the removed-channel count unstated; loss weights not given.
evaluation_limits: Held-out subjects are calibrated on their own data (subset size unstated); null shuffles trials and channels; shuffle count, seeds, split unit and correlation axes not reported; cross-subject linear result given without a number.
deployment_limits: Offline laboratory MEG analysis of 27-s trials; no latency, online or communication test.
scope_limits: 11 trained musicians, two melodies and two poems, listened and imagined, 10 trials each.
task: Map imagined auditory MEG responses to the corresponding listened-response MEG for melodies and spoken poems.
input_modality: Non-invasive MEG (KIT, 157 axial gradiometers) during listening and auditory imagery.
sensor_hardware: Whole-head KIT MEG with 157 axial gradiometers; 1 kHz sampling, online 500-Hz low-pass and 60-Hz notch; magnetically shielded room.
output_type: Predicted listened-response MEG time series; no decoded audio, transcript, or direct communication output is reported.
vocabulary_type: Fixed musical and spoken-poem stimuli, repeatedly cued; no unseen content.
vocabulary_size: 4 stimuli (2 melodies, 2 poem excerpts); no lexical vocabulary size reported.
metrics: Eight-condition correlation classification 50.7% (SEM 4.1%, chance 12.5%); held-out-subject CNN mean r 0.0113 vs null 0.0063, true above null for all but two subjects.
evaluation_mode: Leave-one-trial-out ridge regression per subject; leave-one-subject-out CNN with held-out-subject calibration; null retrained on trial- and channel-shuffled data; group Wilcoxon signed-rank test on Fisher-transformed correlations.

evidence.statement: Eleven trained musicians (7 male) listened to and imagined two melodies and two poem excerpts, 10 trials of 27 s per stimulus and mode, 80 trials each (Sec. II).
Correlation-based classification over eight conditions (listened or imagined x four stimuli) averages 50.7% (SEM 4.1%, chance 12.5%); this separates conditions, not stimulus content (Sec. IV).
The CNN is a 1-D temporal encoder-decoder followed by a per-subject kernel-size-1 calibration layer, predicting listened MEG from imagined MEG (Sec. V-B, Fig. 5).

On held-out subjects calibrated on part of their own data, mean r is 0.0113 for the true model and 0.0063 for the shuffled null, Wilcoxon p << 0.01; the true model exceeds null for all but two subjects (Sec. V-B, Fig. 7).
evidence.section_or_location: Section V.B, held-out-subject results and Figure 7, PDF p.5

evidence.statement: The calibration subset size and its split unit relative to test data are not reported (Sec. V-B).
evidence.section_or_location: CNN training and calibration, PDF pp.4–5

evidence.statement: Fig. 5 shows 155 input channels against 157 recorded gradiometers; the removed channels are not counted (Sec. II, Fig. 5).
evidence.section_or_location: Sections II–III and Figure 5, PDF pp.3–4

evidence.statement: Offline analysis of full 27-s trials; no real-time, portable or communication evaluation is reported.
evidence.section_or_location: Experimental Paradigm, PDF pp.2–3; CNN architecture/results, PDF pp.4–5

evidence.statement: The authors claim imagined responses can be transformed into listened-response space and that the CNN transfers to unseen subjects (Abstract, Sec. VI).
KIT whole-head MEG with 157 axial gradiometers at 1 kHz; preprocessing 0.1-8 Hz band-pass, first seven DSS components, per-channel z-score, 100 Hz (Sec. II-III).

Per-subject ridge regression with 500-ms windows and 100-ms steps, leave-one-trial-out, beats a shuffled null (Wilcoxon p << 0.001); cross-subject training is described as poor with no number (Sec. V-A, Fig. 3).
evidence.section_or_location: Section V.A and Figure 3, PDF p.3

evidence.statement: The shared CNN uses an 80-20 train-validation split of the other subjects, Adam 10^-4, kernel 7, dropout 0.1 and early stopping, with MSE, negative-correlation, temporal-difference and spectral losses; the null shuffles trial order and channel assignment (Sec. V-B).
Loss weights were set by an ablation that is not reported; outputs are listened MEG responses, with no word, audio or communication measure (Sec. V-B, VI).
evidence.section_or_location: Section V.B (loss weights and results) and Section VI, PDF pp.4–5

en.summary: Mapping imagined onto listened MEG (M06) is ahead in design, but the subject-calibrated CNN gain is unproven: no ablation, a channel-shuffling null, and r 0.0113 against 0.0063.
en.sensor: Whole-head KIT MEG, 157 axial gradiometers
en.task: Mapping imagined to listened auditory MEG
en.speaker: Both
en.key_result: 8-condition accuracy 50.7% (chance 12.5%); CNN mean r 0.0113 vs control 0.0063
en.limitations: Very small correlations, no speech or text reconstruction, 11 trained musicians in a shielded room, and incomplete implementation and split details.

title: A cross-species neural foundation model for end-to-end speech decoding
expert_take_short: Cascaded decoding with the pretrained encoder is a strong standard result; the end-to-end audio-LLM path beats the prior end-to-end entry but trails RNN cascades, and the cross-species gain is small.
expert_take_long: The cascaded result holds: the new encoder gives the lowest non-ensembled WER on both Brain-to-Text holdouts with the field's usual 5-gram plus LLM-rescoring decoder. The end-to-end audio-LLM decoder improves on the prior end-to-end entry (15.67% against 24.69% as single models) but is behind the field's cascades on the same data and behind a concurrent Whisper-based end-to-end decoder; the abstract's headline gain sets an LLM-merged ensemble against a non-ensembled entry. Monkey data add little over human pretraining, with no seeds reported. Pretraining can include the benchmark holdout recordings, and removing the fine-tuning participants' data from pretraining raises cascaded WER by 7-14% relative.
expert_true_value: A cross-species self-supervised encoder gives the lowest single-model WER on both Brain-to-Text holdouts when paired with the field's standard 5-gram plus LLM-rescoring decoder; the end-to-end audio-LLM path improves on the prior end-to-end entry but stays behind earlier RNN cascades.
canon_before: Prior speech BCIs relied on cascaded RNN encoders decoding phonemes combined with n-gram language models. Limited or no large scale pretraining, transformers not widely used, end-to-end speech decoding with LLMs was emerging but still relied on RNNs and lacked large-scale neural data integration.
delta_from_canon: Adds masked self-supervised pretraining on 366.8 hours of human and monkey Utah-array data and an audio-LLM end-to-end decoder with contrastive alignment. The pretraining improves the cascade; the monkey data add little; the end-to-end decoder improves on the earlier end-to-end entry (15.67% vs 24.69% single model) but not on cascades.
position_in_field: Standard cascaded design with a stronger pretrained encoder; for end-to-end decoding, better than the prior end-to-end entry but behind the field's cascades.
practical_value: The cascaded encoder is a usable improvement for offline benchmarks; the end-to-end path is slower (0.95 s per sentence), uses a bidirectional encoder unfit for online use, and is behind a concurrent Whisper-based decoder, so it is not yet a practical replacement.
axes_moved: Encoder pretraining moved to pooled cross-species self-supervision; an end-to-end audio-LLM decoder was added alongside the cascaded decoder.
axes_unresolved: Remaining generalization to unseen subjects is unclear; full real-time suitability and robust long-term deployment with larger LLMs remain open; addressing neural plasticity and co-adaptation is future work.
axes_regressed: Decoding latency for end-to-end method is slower (approx. 0.95s per sentence) than cascaded (0.24s); bidirectional attention in encoder limits online real-time decoding currently.
technical_limits: End-to-end latency and computational requirements; bidirectional attention inhibits online decoding; large pretrained LLMs require substantial resources; need for large labeled and unlabeled datasets; limited real-time applicability currently.
evaluation_limits: Evaluations focused on two human participants (T12, T15) and limited imagined speech vocabulary; unknown performance on larger, more diverse subject sets; small batch sizes for contrastive learning may limit modality alignment effectiveness; inference strategies like nucleus sampling could be further optimized.
deployment_limits: End-to-end model latency (~0.95s per sentence) and requirement for bidirectional attention constrain real-time deployment; larger LLMs unsuitable for on-device use; dependency on large unlabeled and labeled datasets for pretraining and fine-tuning.
scope_limits: Limited to Utah array intracortical neural recordings, tested only on two human participants and associated monkey data; generalization to other populations or hardware untested.
input_modality: electrophysiological neural spiking activity (Utah arrays)
sensor_hardware: Utah microelectrode arrays with thresholded spikes and spike-band power (SBP) features
vocabulary_type: natural language English text
vocabulary_size: Attempted-speech holdout vocabulary condition not stated per table; 50 words for imagined speech.
metrics: WER on the Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 hidden-label holdouts (single models and LLM-merged ensembles); validation PER and WER for ablations, one value per condition without seeds; imagined-speech WER on a 50-word set; latency per sentence (0.95 s end-to-end, 0.24 s cascaded).
evaluation_mode: Quantitative performance evaluation on held-out datasets (word error rate), ablation studies, representational similarity analysis, and decoding error analyses.

evidence.statement: We introduce an end-to-end BraIn-to-Text (BIT) framework that translates neural activity into coherent sentences using a single differentiable neural network with a cross-task, cross-species pretrained neural encoder, supporting both attempted and imagined speech decoding.
BIT Cascaded achieves state-of-the-art WER of 6.35% on Brain-to-Text ’24 hold-out, outperforming previous best 7.98%, and BIT End-to-End reduces prior end-to-end WER from 24.69% to 10.22%.
The neural encoder is a transformer pretrained with self-supervised masked modeling on 367 hours of human and monkey Utah array neural data across speech and motor tasks.

Speech decoding was conducted on Brain-to-Text Benchmark ’24 and ’25 intracortical Utah array datasets with two human participants (T12 and T15) for attempted speech and a smaller imagined speech dataset involving the same individuals.
Phoneme decoding uses a 41-token vocabulary including phonemes plus blank and silence tokens, with phoneme error rates (PER) correlated with word error rates (WER) after decoding.

End-to-end decoding requires about 0.95 seconds per sentence on average, slower than cascaded decoding at 0.24 seconds, limiting real-time applicability; bidirectional attention in the neural encoder is unsuitable for online decoding.
LLMs of larger scale than 1.5B parameters used here cannot run on-device, limiting mobile real-time applications.

This work combines cross-species, cross-task transformer-based self-supervised pretraining with an audio-LLM end-to-end decoder for neural speech decoding, a novel integration beyond prior cascaded, RNN-based, or purely task-specific models.

Evaluations were conducted on two particular human participants (T12 and T15) for attempted speech with large vocabularies and on imagined speech with a reduced 50-word vocabulary, limiting generalization scope.
Contrastive learning is employed to align neural and text embeddings in a shared latent space to improve cross-modal alignment and decoding performance.
This model was pretrained on thresholded spikes and spike-band power (SBP) features from Utah array intracortical recordings.

en.summary: Cascaded decoding with the pretrained encoder is a strong standard result; the end-to-end audio-LLM path beats the prior end-to-end entry but trails RNN cascades, and the cross-species gain is small.
en.sensor: Intracortical Utah arrays in ventral motor cortex (128 electrodes for T12, 256 for T15); thresholded spikes and spike-band power
en.task: Sentence decoding from attempted speech (Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 holdouts) and imagined speech (50-word set)
en.vocabulary: Large-vocabulary attempted-speech sentences; 50 words for imagined speech
en.speaker: Two participants (T12, T15); pretraining also on other human and monkey recordings
en.session: T12: 25 sessions over four months; T15: 45 sessions over 20 months
en.key_result: Cascaded decoding with the pretrained encoder reaches 6.35% (Brain-to-Text '24) and 4.06% ('25) holdout WER as single models, below every non-ensembled entry, and 5.10% and 1.76% with LLM-merged ensembles. The single end-to-end audio-LLM model reaches 15.67% and 11.06%: better than the prior end-to-end entry (24.69%) but behind the RNN baselines (9.76%, 6.67%); the headline 24.69% to 10.22% uses a 10-model ensemble.
en.limitations: Cross-species gain is small (validation PER 15.95% to 14.39% and 7.61% to 7.12%, one value per cell without seeds); pretraining can include the benchmark holdout recordings, and removing the fine-tuning participants' data from pretraining raises cascaded WER to 7.24% and 4.36%; ablations report no seeds or intervals; imagined speech is a 50-word task without chance baseline or test counts; end-to-end takes 0.95 s per sentence (cascaded 0.24 s) with a bidirectional encoder unsuitable for online decoding.

title: A Parallel Ultra-Low Power Silent Speech Interface based on a Wearable, Fully-dry EMG Neckband
expert_take_short: 完全乾式の首輪型筋電計測で、健康な1人の無声8語分類は68±3%。装着し直した未学習セッションでは54±7%に下がる。22.2mWは計測・無線通信の値で、自由会話や端末内実時間認識の完成を示すものではない。
expert_take_long: この研究の価値は、首に巻く布製の装置で湿式参照電極も不要にし、計測・通信の省電力化と装着し直しの問題を同時に扱った点にある。14差動チャネルの筋電を取得し、健康な1人が8種類の命令語を通常発話または無声調音する。各条件3セッション・3360発話を収録し、画面提示後の最初の1.4秒から特徴量を作ってRandom Forestで分類する。全セッションを混ぜた5分割評価では通常発話87±3%、無声68±3%だが、装着し直した1セッションを丸ごと評価用にすると、それぞれ64±18%、54±7%に下がる。±は著者の標準偏差であり、参加者間のばらつきではない。8択の偶然水準12.5%を上回っていても、未知の装着条件に十分強い、あるいは日常の意思伝達に使えるとまではいえない。報告された22.2mWは継続計測とBluetooth Low Energyによる通信の消費電力で、首輪上の認識や受信側を含むシステム全体の電力・電池持続時間ではない。200ミリ秒ごとの区間も特徴抽出の単位であり、7区間を連結するため200ミリ秒で命令を出す実時間実験とは異なる。新しい筋電原理や自由文の復号ではなく、完全乾式の装着型機器の設計と、その再装着時の限界を把握するための初期検証として読むのが適切である。
expert_true_value: 乾式電極・無線・省電力の計測装置を、単なる分類精度だけでなく再装着時の性能低下と併せて評価できる点。
canon_before: 表面筋電による無声発話分類と首輪型・無線計測は既存研究にある。本論文は、顔への電極装着、湿式参照電極、計測基板、装着位置の変化を実用化上の課題として位置付ける。
delta_from_canon: 27個の接続部を持つ布製首輪に乾式電極を取り付け、14差動チャネルの筋電をBioGAP-Ultraで取得する。分類法の刷新より、湿式参照を不要にする構成と、同一人物の装着し直しを切り分けた評価が中心。
position_in_field: 表面筋電を用いる首輪型の閉語彙命令認識。アルゴリズム競争より、完全乾式の電極・計測機器と同一人物のセッション変動の研究に位置付けられる。
practical_value: 再装着を前提とする装着型の無声命令入力装置を設計する際に、計測電力と未学習セッションの精度を分けて検討する資料になる。
axes_moved: 乾式の参照電極を含む首輪型計測、計測・通信の消費電力、装着し直したセッションを分けた評価。
axes_unresolved: 人数・語彙の拡張、連続動作からの発話検出、端末内認識、実時間遅延、長時間装着、歩行や日常動作、患者での意思伝達。
axes_regressed: 同じ3セッションを学習・評価の双方に含む分割から、1セッションを丸ごと未学習にする分割へ変えると、無声時68±3%から54±7%、通常発話87±3%から64±18%へ下がる。
technical_limits: 発話開始を画面提示で揃え、最初の1.4秒だけを処理する。自然な連続信号からの発話区間検出、無入力時の誤作動、会話中の遷移、装置上での推論性能は示されない。
evaluation_limits: 1人の反復収録なので参加者間のばらつきは測れない。全セッション混合の5分割評価は新しい装着セッションへの汎化ではない。本文は平均と標準偏差を報告するが、有意差検定、乱数・ソフトウェア版、独立した再現実験は示さない。
deployment_limits: 実験は1人への画面提示に同期した単語収録。受信・提示にノートパソコンを使い、搭載GAP9での認識実行は報告されない。歩行、食事、自然な会話、長時間の快適性、患者での使用は未検証。
scope_limits: arXiv 2509.21964v1の全4ページを読み、図1–4をPDF表示でも確認した。引用先の装置論文を独立に精査した結果ではなく、本論文に記載された構成と結果を評価する。コード実行、独立再現、追加資料の公開状況確認はしていない。
task: 通常発話および無声調音の8語命令分類。提示された単語区間を分類する閉語彙課題。
input_modality: 首の表面筋電。通常発話と無声調音を別条件として収録する。脳波や想像発話の計測ではない。
sensor_hardware: 布製首輪、乾式SoftPulse電極、27接続部、前面10差動対と左右各2差動チャネルの計14チャネル、後面4電極を短絡した接地。BioGAP-UltraはGAP9、nRF5340、ADS1298を2個搭載する。計測基板は16差動チャネル対応だが首輪で用いるのは14。24ビット、増幅率12、500samples/s。
body_site: throat; 首の前面・側面の皮膚、後面の接地電極
output_type: 8命令語のクラスラベル。連続文字列や音声波形を生成する実験ではない。
vocabulary_type: 移動や制御を想定した固定8命令語。自由文・開語彙ではない。
vocabulary_size: 8語：up, down, left, right, forward, backward, go, stop。
metrics: 全セッション混合・層化5分割の正解率：通常発話87±3%、無声68±3%。leave-one-session-out：通常発話64±18%、無声54±7%。通常発話のセッション内モデルの平均は85±7%、初回セッションは74%。8クラスの偶然水準は12.5%。±は著者記載の標準偏差。継続計測とBLE通信の電力は22.2mW。いずれも著者報告で独立再現ではない。
evaluation_mode: セッション内の7バッチを使う7分割交差検証、全3セッションを混ぜて無作為化した層化5分割交差検証、2セッションで学習し残る1セッションで評価するleave-one-session-out。通常発話と無声調音を区別し、語別と全体の正解率を報告する。

evidence.statement: 主眼は14チャネルの完全乾式筋電首輪、BioGAP-Ultraの低消費電力計測・通信、再装着を伴う評価であり、新しい認識原理ではない。
evidence.section_or_location: p.1, Section I contribution bullets; pp.1–2, Section II-A/B/E

evidence.statement: 首輪は27接続部を備え、前面10差動対と左右各2チャネルを用いる。後面の4接地電極は電気的に短絡される。基板の16チャネル対応と首輪の14チャネルを区別する。
BioGAP-UltraはGAP9、nRF5340、ADS1298を2個含み、信号を増幅率12・500samples/sで取得する。貢献の記述は24ビット計測とする。
evidence.section_or_location: p.1, Section I contribution bullets; p.2, Section II-B and Figure 1(d)

evidence.statement: 対象は健康な1人で、up/down/left/right/forward/backward/go/stopの8語を通常発話と無声調音で収録する。未学習人物や未知語の認識ではない。
各条件3セッション・各7バッチ・各語20反復で3360発話を収録する。提示後4秒の調音と1秒の休止、バッチ約14分と5分休憩を設け、セッション前に水で皮膚を清拭し首輪を付け直す。
20Hz・4次の零位相高域通過と50Hzノッチの後、最初の1.4秒を7個の重ならない200ms窓に分け、特徴量を連結して1発話を表す。
時間・周波数領域およびdb4ウェーブレットの特徴を使い、scikit-learnの既定設定のRandom Forestで8クラス分類する。特徴重要度に支配的な項目がないため全特徴を保持する。
全セッション混合の層化5分割では各分割に全セッションが含まれる。leave-one-session-outは2セッションで学習し残る1セッションを評価するため、未知の人物を試す方式ではない。
evidence.section_or_location: p.2, Section II-E, Global model and Leave-one-session-out

evidence.statement: 通常発話はセッション内モデルの平均85±7%、初回74%、全セッション混合87±3%、セッション除外64±18%と報告される。8クラスの偶然水準は12.5%。
無声調音の全セッション混合は68±3%、セッション除外は54±7%。著者は評価指標を正解率の平均と標準偏差と記載する。1人の実験なので参加者間標準偏差ではない。
evidence.section_or_location: p.2, Section II-E; p.3, Section III-B and Figure 4(b,c)

evidence.statement: 22.2mWは継続的なデータ取得とBLE無線通信の電力として報告される。GAP9での分類実行や受信側を含む全体電力、電池持続時間は報告されない。
evidence.section_or_location: p.1, Section I contribution bullets; p.2, Section II-B/C/E; p.3, Section IV

evidence.statement: 1人の提示同期・8語分類であり、自由文、患者、多人数、歩行、長時間装着、連続信号中の無入力や発話開始検出は評価しない。語彙と人数の拡張は今後の課題とされる。
evidence.section_or_location: p.2, Section II-C/D/E; p.3, Section IV future work

evidence.statement: 無声での低下を活動筋数の減少に帰し、初回の低さを経験不足に帰す記述は著者の解釈である。要因を分離する対照実験や有意差検定は本文に示されない。
200msは特徴抽出の窓長であり、7窓を連結する1.4秒の発話表現を使う。無線収録の実現を、200msの端末内オンライン認識が実証されたことと読み替えられない。
先行研究の93%や89.6%との比較は語彙やクラス数、装置が異なると本文自身が述べる。同条件の直接比較や性能優位を示す試験ではない。
装着し直したセッションでの低下は測定されているが、全セッション混合の高い正解率や偶然水準超えだけで日常生活の信頼性・多人数汎化は保証できない。
evidence.section_or_location: p.2, Section II-C/E; p.3, Section III and Figures 3–4

en.summary: A fully dry wearable EMG neckband with ultra-low-power BioGAP-Ultra classifies 8 silently articulated words for one healthy user at 68% accuracy, dropping to 54% on an unseen re-wearing session; acquisition plus BLE uses 22.2 mW.
en.sensor: Dry-electrode textile neckband, 14-channel EMG
en.speaker: Speaker-dependent
en.key_result: Silent 68% (pooled 5-fold), 54% leave-one-session-out, chance 12.5%
en.limitations: Single participant, cue-aligned 1.4 s segments, no on-device inference reported, and no walking, natural conversation or patient testing.

title: A Silent Speech Decoding System from EEG and EMG with Heterogenous Electrode Configurations
expert_take_short: Pooled EEG/EMG pretraining lifts 64-word accuracy, but each test subject's training sessions, the patient's included, are in pretraining; the coordinate kernel is neither new nor best.
expert_take_long: The paper changes the input layer for heterogeneous electrode layouts (M06) and pooled multi-subject, multi-task pretraining with calibration (M03); both are standard. Coordinate-conditioned input layers predate it, and its proposed kernel is beaten by a fixed per-subject layer. The gains (70.1% to 95.3% healthy, 13.2% to 54.5% for one patient) hold within the paper, but the pretraining set contains every subject's word-task training sessions, the patient's 16 included, and data volume grows with devices, tasks and supervision at once. No EEG-only or EMG-only model is reported. New-user generalization is an untabulated calibration curve, and other patients are untested.
expert_true_value: A controlled comparison of four ways to feed EEG and EMG from different electrode layouts into one model, showing that pooled pretraining with a per-subject input layer lifts 64-word silent accuracy; it does not show transfer from healthy data to unseen users or patients.
canon_before: Non-invasive speech decoders were mostly trained per subject on one fixed montage. Input layers conditioned on sensor positions (spatial attention, Defossez et al. 2023) and on MNI electrode coordinates across ECoG and sEEG layouts (Chen et al. 2024) already existed, as did per-subject input layers.
delta_from_canon: Pools 220 hours of EEG and EMG from five electrode configurations and several tasks into one Conformer with multi-task supervision, and compares pooling, electrode-specific, subject-specific and coordinate-kernel tokenizers on a 64-word Japanese silent task including one patient.
position_in_field: Standard on the input layer (M06) and on pooled pretraining with calibration (M03): coordinate-conditioned mapping predates it and the proposed kernel is beaten by a per-subject layer; the evaluation keeps each test subject's training sessions, the patient's included, in pretraining.
practical_value: A recipe for reusing EEG and EMG recorded with different devices and layouts to support a small amount of patient data; the benefit for everyday communication is not measured.
axes_moved: With the subject-specific tokenizer and 220 h of pooled data, 64-word accuracy rises from 70.1% to 95.3% (healthy mean) and from 13.2% to 54.5% (one patient) against individual-data baselines.
axes_unresolved: Transfer to users and patients absent from pretraining; contribution of EEG versus EMG; zero-shot use of an unseen electrode layout; open vocabulary and sentences; long-term stability; clinical benefit.
axes_regressed: Training time grows from about 2 hours per split to about 4 days on one H100; the proposed coordinate kernel does not beat the subject-specific layer, and pooling (GAP) fails in English transfer at 100% PER against 61.5% from scratch.
technical_limits: No EEG-only or EMG-only model, so the signal carrying the decoding is not identified. Data volume grows together with devices, tasks and supervision. The subject-specific tokenizer needs a layer per user, so a new user needs calibration. The authors' explanations of the patient's lower accuracy are not tested.
evaluation_limits: Per-participant session split (sessions 1-16 train, 17-18 validation, 19-20 test) with all subjects' word-task training sessions, the patient's included, in pretraining. One patient. No seed count or repeated runs; the +/-17.1 on the baseline is undefined. Calibration values appear only in Fig. 3. English transfer is one speaker's facial EMG with no split or uncertainty reported, so it says nothing about EEG.
deployment_limits: Laboratory recording with many scalp and facial electrodes and on-screen timing cues; a 27 Hz notch for medical-device interference in the patient. 57 ms per 3.3 s sample on unstated hardware is throughput, not end-to-end latency; no online use.
scope_limits: Japanese prompted silent words (64 classes) from eight healthy participants and one ventilator-dependent patient; English phoneme decoding on one speaker's facial EMG as a transfer test.
task: Cued silent Japanese 64-word classification, with calibration to a novel healthy participant and to new-day patient data, and English phoneme decoding from facial EMG as transfer; not inner speech.
input_modality: Non-invasive scalp EEG and surface facial EMG; audio and text of vocalized data serve only as training supervision; English transfer uses facial EMG only.
sensor_hardware: Main recordings: eego sports, 63 EEG and 5 bipolar EMG channels at 2048 Hz. Pretraining also uses g.Pangolin (128 EEG, 3 EMG channels) and g.SCARABEO (62 EEG, 3 EMG channels) at 1024 Hz.
body_site: Scalp; cheek, upper and lower mouth, chin and throat; in the patient the throat pair is moved above and below an eye because of medical equipment.
output_type: 64-word class label for the main evaluation; multi-task heads also predict audio latents and Japanese mora sequences; English phoneme sequences in transfer.
vocabulary_type: Closed set of Japanese words; English transfer is phoneme decoding, not word accuracy.
vocabulary_size: 64 words for classification; 153 Japanese sentences recorded (267-item sentence vocabulary in Table 1); the English dataset's 9,828-word vocabulary is not a class count.
metrics: 64-word accuracy with the subject-specific tokenizer on all data: 95.3 +/- 2.6% healthy mean (95% bootstrap CI), 54.5% patient; individual-data baselines 70.1 +/- 17.1% and 13.2%; chance 1.6%. English PER: scratch 61.5, GAP 100, ES 49.5, SS 50.0, OTFK 55.8.
evaluation_mode: Offline fixed 64-word classification on a per-participant session split; calibration curves for a novel healthy participant and new-day patient data; English phoneme error rate.

evidence.statement: Main recordings come from eight healthy participants and one patient with a progressive neuromuscular disease who depends on a ventilator and cannot vocalize; the throat EMG pair is moved above and below an eye because of medical equipment.

Participants read 64 patient-selected Japanese words to on-screen timing cues; healthy participants did 20 word and 2 sentence sessions, the patient 20 silent word sessions, some cut short by fatigue. No inner-speech task.

Four tokenizers are compared: global average pooling (GAP), electrode-specific layers (ES), subject-specific layers (SS) and an on-the-fly kernel (OTFK) computed from 3D electrode coordinates with a positional encoding and a Transformer layer.
The model has about 18.5M parameters: tokenizer, 11-layer Conformer and heads for words, moras and audio latents, with each loss applied where its supervision exists.

'word all' is 16.1 h over two configurations, 'eego all' 76.9 h over three, 'all' 220 h over five, mixing silent and vocalized words, sentences and vocalized-only speech; most of the 220 h is not silent patient data.

Each participant's silent word task uses sessions 1-16 for training, 17-18 for validation and 19-20 for testing with equal word frequencies; the main result is a within-participant session split, not a test on an unseen patient.

SS trained on 'all' reaches 95.3 +/- 2.6% (healthy mean, 95% bootstrap CI) and 54.5% (patient), against individual-data baselines of 70.1 +/- 17.1% and 13.2%; chance is 1.6%. The best mean accuracy comes from SS, not OTFK.

The novel healthy participant's 15 sessions use 1-12 incrementally for calibration, 13 for validation and 14-15 for testing; patient new-day data span three days at least a week apart, 6-7 sessions per day, added to the 16 pretraining sessions.
In Fig. 3(a) the novel healthy participant exceeds 80% after calibration, while new-day patient accuracy in Fig. 3(b) stays well below; the 80% figure does not apply to the patient.
evidence.section_or_location: p.4, Figure 3(a) healthy participant, Figure 3(b) patient, and Section 4.2; panels visually checked

evidence.statement: English transfer uses an existing single-speaker dataset of 19 h of 8-channel facial EMG with a 9,828-word vocabulary, samples up to 15 s; the Japanese mora head is replaced by an English phoneme head and fine-tuned.
English PER is 61.5 from scratch, 100 with GAP, 49.5 with ES, 50.0 with SS and 55.8 with OTFK (lower is better); not every tokenizer helps, and this is not word or sentence accuracy.
evidence.section_or_location: p.4, Table 2 and Section 4.2; table visually checked

evidence.statement: Training takes about 2 hours per split for 'word' and about 4 days for 'all' on an H100; mean inference is 57 ms for 3.3 s samples, without the latency of recording, segmentation, preprocessing or response.

EEG: 50 Hz notch, common average reference, 2-120 Hz band-pass, resampling to 240 Hz; EMG the same without common average reference; an extra 27 Hz notch for medical-device interference in the patient.

The data-size comparison (Fig. 2, Table 1) changes speakers, tasks, devices and electrode layouts along with hours, and no EEG-only or EMG-only model is given, so the gain cannot be assigned to one signal or to OTFK.
evidence.section_or_location: pp.2–4, Figure 1, Table 1, Sections 3.2 and 4.1, Figure 2

evidence.statement: The authors attribute the patient's lower accuracy to mouth movements unlike the healthy data and to words indistinguishable in EMG, but test neither cause.
The authors state that generalization to other patients could not be confirmed because patient data are hard to collect, and leave language-model sentence decoding to future work.

The paper does not give trial lists, seeds, loss weights, the English split and decoder details, or how a subject-specific layer is initialized for a new user, so the text alone does not support reproduction.
evidence.section_or_location: pp.2–4, Sections 2.3–2.5 and 3.2–4.2; five-page v1 scope

evidence.statement: Main recordings use 63 EEG and 5 EMG channels at 2048 Hz; pooled data add devices with 128 or 62 EEG channels and 3 EMG channels. The 153 Japanese sentences, the 267-item sentence vocabulary and the 9,828 English words are separate from the 64 classes.

en.summary: Pooled EEG/EMG pretraining lifts 64-word accuracy, but each test subject's training sessions, the patient's included, are in pretraining; the coordinate kernel is neither new nor best.
en.sensor: 63-channel scalp EEG plus 5 bipolar facial EMG channels (eego sports); pretraining also on g.Pangolin and g.SCARABEO EEG with 3 EMG channels
en.task: Closed-set silent word classification (64 Japanese words); English phoneme decoding as a transfer test
en.vocabulary: 64 Japanese words; English transfer set with a 9,828-word vocabulary
en.speaker: Eight healthy participants and one patient; per-participant session split; one novel healthy participant for calibration
en.session: Sessions 1-16 train, 17-18 validation, 19-20 test per participant; patient new-day data over three days
en.key_result: 64-word accuracy 95.3% healthy (vs 70.1% individual-data baseline) and 54.5% patient (vs 13.2%; chance 1.6%) with the subject-specific tokenizer pretrained on 220 h
en.limitations: Test subjects' training sessions, including the patient's, are in the pretraining data; one patient; no EEG-only or EMG-only model; no seed count; data volume confounded with devices and tasks; calibration values only in a figure; English transfer is EMG only.

title: An Introduction to Silent Paralinguistics
expert_take_short: 声を出さない会話で、言葉だけでなく感情や話し方も伝えるための総説。研究課題の整理は有用だが、感情の復元精度や実用効果を新たに実証した論文ではない。
expert_take_long: この論文の価値は、声を出さずに言葉を伝える技術を、文字や音声の内容が合うだけでなく、本人の感情や話し方まで伝えられるかという問いに広げた点にある。生体信号から感情などを直接推定する経路と、いったん作った音響特徴から推定する経路を分け、音声合成との接続を整理する。ただし、新しい認識装置を実験した論文ではない。表IIは声を出して収録した研究をまとめ、表IIIは無声発話を含む3件の先行研究を挙げる。筋電から話者・発話様式を識別する研究、強勢を扱う研究、脳内電極で速度や疑問文の抑揚などを扱う研究は、同じ感情認識課題ではなく、一つの精度にまとめられない。引用データの8話者・63セッションも本論文が新たに評価した集団ではない。特に重要なのは、無声発話では声の高さを直接測った正解がなく、抑揚情報がどこまで残るかも未解明だという指摘である。生成音声に感情らしい特徴を付けられても、それが本人の意図した表現を復元した証拠にはならない。顔画像や合成音声を正解の代わりに使う提案も、その対応関係を別に検証する必要がある。文献収集の再現手順、共通条件の比較、患者や自然会話での新規評価はない。また、侵襲的な信号を不適としながら脳内電極の研究を主要例に含めており、領域の対象範囲には整理の余地がある。研究計画の入口として有用だが、無声時の感情復元精度、自然さの改善、精神的健康への効果を実証済みと読むべきではない。
expert_true_value: 内容の正しさと表現の正しさを切り分け、無声時の正解データと本人の意図の確認を中心課題として見えるようにすること。
canon_before: 本稿が比較する既存総説は、無声発話インターフェース、生体信号、感情などの推定、音声認識、音声変換を主に別々に扱う。一方、話者や発話様式を筋電から推定する先行研究自体は本稿の表IIIにも存在する。
delta_from_canon: 無声発話の内容復元、非言語的な特徴の推定、表現豊かな音声合成を一つの研究課題として結び付け、生体信号から直接推定する経路と、生成した音響特徴を経由する経路を分ける。
position_in_field: 無声発話インターフェース、感情などの自動推定、表現豊かな音声合成の接点を整理する総説。
practical_value: 研究課題、計測手段、正解データ、合成音声の評価を検討するための入口。装置選定の性能ランキングや臨床効果の根拠には使えない。
axes_moved: 研究課題の整理。何を言ったかの復元に加え、どう伝えるかを無声発話の評価対象に置く。
axes_unresolved: 無声時の感情・抑揚の正解の定義、実際に残る生理的情報、未知話者・言語・文化への一般化、自然会話と患者での検証、合成音声の表現が本人の意図に一致するか。
axes_regressed: 新規システムの比較実験がないため性能の後退は評価対象外。侵襲的な計測を不適とする説明と、それを主要な先行例に含める整理には不整合がある。
technical_limits: 無声時の声の高さには実測の正解がなく、抑揚情報の保持も未解明。間接経路は生体信号から音響特徴への変換に依存する。音響的類似性だけでは人が意図した表現を聞き取れるとは保証できない。
evaluation_limits: 検索式、検索日、採否基準、選別件数、研究の質の評価を再現できる文献収集手順は示されない。共通データでの再評価、統合した効果量、新規の定量評価もない。引用研究の結果をこの総説の性能値として移してはいけない。
deployment_limits: 新規の装着装置、実環境評価、患者試験はない。論文中の非侵襲・侵襲・口内装着などの計測手段は異なる利用条件を持ち、同じ実用性で扱えない。
scope_limits: 2025年8月25日のarXiv v1、全21ページを対象とする総説の評価。引用研究全件の独立検証や最新文献への更新ではない。通常の有声発話や音楽・動画視聴中の感情研究も背景として含む。
input_modality: 生体信号全般の総説。脳波、脳血流に関わる光計測、皮質表面・脳内電極、表面筋電、口や舌の磁気計測、声帯接触の電気的計測、顔動画、舌の超音波画像を扱う。
sensor_hardware: 単一の新規装置はない。表面脳波、近赤外分光計測、皮質表面電極、脳内電極、表面筋電、電磁・永久磁石式調音計測、声門電気計測、動画、超音波画像などの既存手段を概説する。
body_site: brain; face; jaw; lip; throat; tongue; oral-cavity
output_type: 文献整理と研究方針。目指す出力は感情などの特徴を反映した合成音声・注釈付き文字であり、本稿が生成・評価した成果物ではない。
vocabulary_type: 異なる既存課題を扱う総説であり、単一の認識語彙ではない。
vocabulary_size: 本総説に単一の評価語彙はない。
metrics: 本総説としての新規の精度、誤り率、遅延、自然さの評点は報告なし。表IIIの3件は既存研究の分類であり、共通条件の成績表ではない。EMG-UKAの8話者・63セッションは引用データの記述。
evaluation_mode: 関連技術と既存研究を整理する叙述的総説。新規実験、統一ベンチマーク、定量的な統合分析ではない。

evidence.statement: 本稿は無声発話の生体信号から感情や話者特性などを捉えて表現するSilent Paralinguisticsを定義し、関連技術と研究方針を整理する総説である。
evidence.section_or_location: pp.1–2 Abstract, I Introduction, II-A Definition; p.14 VIII Conclusion

evidence.statement: 長期的な特徴、中間的な状態、短期的な状態を区分し、年齢・性格、眠気、感情などを例にする。
evidence.section_or_location: p.2 II-A; p.8 Fig.3 and caption

evidence.statement: 直接経路は生体信号から非言語的特徴を推定して生成音響特徴と組み合わせる。間接経路はまず生体信号から音響特徴を作り、その特徴から非言語的情報を推定する。図1は提案する処理の整理であり、両経路の比較実験ではない。
表IIは有声発話中に収録した生体信号の研究であり、筋電、声門電気計測、電磁調音計測、超音波から声の高さや感情などを扱う。無声発話の実証一覧ではない。
evidence.section_or_location: pp.9–11 V-B; p.10 Table II title and rows

evidence.statement: 表IIIは既存の3研究を整理する。Dienerらは筋電で話者と有声・無声・ささやきの発話様式、Vojtechらは筋電で文字・音声・強勢、Wairagkarらは脳内信号で音声・速度・疑問文の抑揚・声の高さを扱う。
本文が8話者・63セッションと記述するのは引用先のEMG-UKAデータであり、本総説が収録・評価した新しい参加者集団ではない。
evidence.section_or_location: p.12 VII-A Current Research, Diener et al. [295] and corpus [296,297]

evidence.statement: 脳内信号から速度・疑問文の抑揚・声の高さを扱う引用研究について、本稿は与えられた文字を読み上げ合成した音声を正解に用いたと記述する。これは無声時の実際の音声を直接測った正解とは異なる。
evidence.section_or_location: p.12 VII-A, Wairagkar et al. [182] discussion

evidence.statement: 無声発話では声の高さの正解が得られず、抑揚情報がどの程度保たれるかも未解明とする。顔画像・動画などから正解情報を付与して合成に組み込む手順は今後の提案である。
evidence.section_or_location: p.13 VII-B1 Paralinguistics in Silent Speech

evidence.statement: MNGU0と引用した超音波研究は単一話者・単一言語であり、複数話者・言語・文化、自然会話や豊かな感情表現を含むデータが必要とする。
喉頭摘出後の利用者では首の筋肉や調音運動が異なり、既存手法の適用範囲を予測しにくいため、実際の患者での研究が必要と記述する。
声に感情を付ける変換では、少ないデータ、演技した感情への偏り、言語・文化の違いが課題であり、出力と目標の音響的な類似性は人の知覚的な一致を保証しない。
III-Aでは皮質表面・脳内電極を侵襲性からSilent Paralinguisticsに不適とする一方、VII-Aと表IIIは脳内電極研究を主要な先行例として含める。対象範囲の説明に不整合がある。
evidence.section_or_location: p.4 III-A ECoG/intracortical paragraphs versus pp.12–13 VII-A and Table III

evidence.statement: II-Bは自然な意思伝達や精神的健康への応用を論じるが、この総説にはそれらを検証する新規の臨床試験や利用者実験はない。用途の期待と効果の実証を分ける必要がある。
evidence.section_or_location: p.2 II-B1–3; p.3 Fig.1 applications; pp.12–14 VII–VIII

evidence.statement: 本稿は文献比較と技術整理を行うが、再現できる検索式・検索日・採否基準・選別件数を報告せず、新規の統一比較実験や定量的な統合分析も示していない。
evidence.section_or_location: p.2 I-A/Table I; pp.3–14 III–VIII and Tables II–III (review structure)

evidence.statement: I-Aはこの話題に既刊研究がないと述べる一方、VII-A・表IIIと文献[295,299]には2020年のTowards/Toward silent paralinguisticsを含む。研究課題の統合と厳密な初出の主張は区別すべきである。
evidence.section_or_location: p.2 I-A; pp.12–13 VII-A/Table III; p.20 references [295,299]

evidence.statement: 有声発話から学んだ声の高さの推定や、生成音声への感情付与は、それだけで無声発話者の意図した感情の復元を示さない。これは本稿の有声・無声の区別、正解不在、知覚評価の限界から導くレビュー上の評価である。
evidence.section_or_location: pp.10,13 Tables II–III; p.12 VI-C; p.13 VII-B1

evidence.statement: 計測、認識・合成、非言語的特徴の推定、感情を付与する音声変換をそれぞれ概説しており、本稿独自のセンサー、学習済みモデル、精度・遅延の結果は提示しない。

en.speaker: Not stated
